results.title: DigitalOcean raises H100, H200 and MI300X GPU Droplet prices about 30%
results.author: Saurabh Khatri
highlights:
# DigitalOcean raises H100, H200 and MI300X GPU Droplet prices about 30%

From August 1, 2026, an H100 GPU Droplet costs $4.41 per GPU-hour on demand instead of $3.39. The L40S and RTX Ada Droplets kept their prices.

By Saurabh Khatri · Published Oct 18, 2026

DigitalOcean raised the on-demand prices of its NVIDIA and AMD GPU Droplets on August 1, 2026. It announced the change in a blog post on July 21, 2026, and gave strong demand for advanced GPU capacity as the reason. The H100, H200 and AMD MI300X Droplets each went up about 30%.

## Old and new prices

On-demand price per GPU per hour. Each of these Droplets comes with 1 or 8 GPUs (the L40S and RTX Ada Droplets with 1).

| GPU | Until July 31 | From August 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA HGX H200 | $3.44 | $4.47 |
| NVIDIA HGX H100 | $3.39 | $4.41 |
| AMD Instinct MI300X | $1.99 | $2.59 |
| NVIDIA L40S | $1.57 | $1.57 |
| NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada | $1.57 | $1.57 |
| NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada | $0.76 | $0.76 |

The old prices are from DigitalOcean’s pricing page as it stood on July 22, 2026, when it said “New on-demand pricing is coming on August 1, 2026.” The page now also lists the AMD Instinct MI325X on demand at $3.80 per GPU-hour.

## Reserved prices

The blog post says 12-month reserved rates changed on August 1 too. If you signed a contract that locks your rate, it stays until the term ends; a renewal moves to the new reserved rate. The page now lists these 12-month reserved prices per GPU-hour: B300 $7.94, H200 $3.40, H100 $3.26, MI350X $4.76, MI325X $2.88 and MI300X $1.91.

## Who pays more

Every GPU Droplet running on or after August 1 is billed at the new rate. The higher charges first appeared on the bill dated September 1, 2026. DigitalOcean told customers who didn’t want the new rate to destroy their GPU Droplets by August 1. Powering a GPU Droplet off doesn’t stop the charges: the FAQ says you pay until you destroy it.

## What to do

If you run an H100 Droplet around the clock, it now costs about $3,220 a month at $4.41 an hour, against about $2,380 at a 12-month reserved rate of $3.26. Compare both with what other GPU clouds charge before you commit for a year.

results.title: NVIDIA GPU Market: Rental Rates Fluctuate, Prices Surge, Depreciation | GG Echo
results.author: Sarah Lin
highlights:
Alright, this convention floor is a madhouse, but the data is coming in, and it’s a mess, just like my brain right now. Okay, so the big story, the one everyone’s whispering about, is this whole GPU depreciation thing, right? The original article from Wccftech, it was talking about how A100, H100, H200 rental rates were pricing upwards, and B200s were just shy of $6 an hour. That was August 3, 2026. But here’s the thing, the market is moving fast, really fast. Some of the newer data, like from Q2 2026, actually shows H100 cloud rental rates fell from around $8 an hour in early 2023 to $1.80-$3.50 an hour.

Spot pricing even hit $1.20 an hour. That’s a pretty big drop, not exactly “pricing upwards” across the board for everything. B200s, the new hotness, their rental rates in Q2 2026 are sitting around $4.50-$7.00 an hour. So that “just shy of $6” from the Wccftech article, it’s still in the ballpark, but it’s a range now, and some providers are even lower. Vast.ai, for example, lists B200s at $4.38 an hour.

Runcrate even has B200 cloud rental from $3.20 an hour. GPUs.io shows a market median of $6.03 an hour across 20 configurations for B200s. So, it’s not a single upward trajectory for all GPUs, and the B200 is definitely seeing some competitive pricing. The H200, which is supposed to bridge the gap between H100 and B200, is going for about $3.00-$4.50 an hour in Q2 2026. Thunder Compute has H100 80GB at $2.19 an hour, and A100 80GB at $1.09 an hour as of August 2, 2026.

Major cloud providers like AWS have cut costs for H100, H200, and A100 instances by up to 45%. This is creating opportunities for developers who were priced out before. The depreciation argument, that’s still a huge deal. Proponents of a longer shelf life, they say these GPUs are useful for more than the traditional 3-year estimate. The rising rental rates for some older GPUs, like the A100s and H100s, earlier in the year, that was bolstering the longer useful life argument.

## Restated Aug 7, 2026

Restated from $6.5175 across 4 providers to $5.2225 across 6.

- Crusoe and Lambda were excluded on 2026-07-29 because a single 30-day editorial-review clock had lapsed, even though the collector was re-reading and confirming both prices every morning and neither price moved during July. Review expiry sheds cheap long-tail neoclouds faster than vendor-fed hyperscalers, so the four-provider sample was biased upward.
- All six constituents were re-verified live on 2026-08-07 and every price reconciled unchanged. The eligibility gate now runs separate clocks for automated price checks and editorial review.
- The superseded figures were $6.52 across 4 providers, published as a 51.92% change from June 30.

## July H100 pricing read

The canonical July snapshot produces a $5.22 median from 6 providers. The published median is +21.74% versus the final June history point.

- Median of one deterministically selected, current, reviewed public on-demand H100 price per provider. Quote-only, unavailable, unapproved, superseded, and expired rows are excluded.
- The headline change combines price observations and sample composition. It should not be read as a pure same-provider market move.
- The historical series did not preserve row-level constituent IDs for the prior report, so a constant-provider comparison cannot be supported without inventing the prior provider set.

results.title: GPU rental prices double in seven months as AI compute demand defies market selloff
results.author: Editorial Team
highlights:
The price of renting a GPU just doubled. Gavin Baker, CIO of Atreides Management, flagged that spot rental prices for the same GPU cluster jumped from just under $2 per hour to nearly $4 over a seven-month stretch, with the observation landing on August 4, 2026.

## The numbers behind the squeeze

Spot GPU rental rates are now running at least 2x higher than contracted rates, based on Baker’s observations from late July 2026.

H100 1-year contract pricing climbed approximately 40% from $1.70 per hour in October 2025 to $2.35 per hour by March 2026.

Baker suspects that spot rates exceeding contracted rates by at least twofold suggests hyperscalers have meaningful pricing power they haven’t fully exercised yet.
